metadata.title: Notes on Perelman's papers
metadata.notes: Massive expository paper (18411 lines, 200+ environments) detailing Perelman's proof of the Poincare and Geometrization Conjectures via Ricci flow with surgery. Extraction captures the high-level structure: the 8 introductory claims, key definitions of functionals/objects (F, W, lambda, kappa-solution, kappa-noncollapsed, Ricci flow with surgery, canonical neighborhoods), the major theorems (no local collapsing, pseudolocality, canonical neighborhood, surgery existence, thick-thin decomposition, II.7.4 graph manifold), and cited prior conjectures (Poincare, Geometrization, Hamilton's program). For tractability, only major proofs are decomposed into proof_steps; routine intermediate lemmas are summarized via `uses` edges to the parent theorems.

nodes.name: Poincare Conjecture
nodes.statement: Every simply-connected closed $3$-manifold is diffeomorphic to $S^3$.

nodes.name: Thurston Geometrization Conjecture
nodes.statement: Every connected orientable closed $3$-manifold $M$ is a connected sum of closed $3$-manifolds $\{M_i\}_{i=1}^n$, each admitting a codimension-$0$ submanifold-with-boundary $G_i$ which is a graph manifold, with $M_i - G_i$ hyperbolic and each torus boundary component of $G_i$ incompressible in $M_i$.

nodes.name: Ricci flow
nodes.section: Section: Ricci flow approach to geometrization
nodes.statement: A smoothly varying family of Riemannian metrics $\{g(t)\}_{t \in [a,b]}$ on a manifold $M$ satisfies the Ricci flow equation if $\frac{\partial g}{\partial t}(t) = -2 \, \Ric(g(t))$ for every $t \in [a,b]$.

nodes.name: Structure of singular set $M-\Omega$ (Claim 1)
nodes.statement: If $T < \infty$ is the blowup time and $\Omega = \{x : \lim_{t \to T^-} R(x,t) < \infty\}$, then $\Omega$ is open, $g(t) \to \overline{g}$ smoothly on compacts of $\Omega$, and there is a geometrically defined neighborhood $U$ of $M - \Omega$ each of whose components is either compact diffeomorphic to $S^1 \times S^2$, $S^1 \times_{\Z_2} S^2$, or $S^3/\Gamma$, or noncompact diffeomorphic to $\R \times S^2$, $\R^3$, or $\R \times_{\Z_2} S^2$.
conclusions: $\Omega$ open and $g(t) \to \overline{g}$ smoothly on compacts of $\Omega$
Neighborhood $U$ of $M-\Omega$ has components of seven explicit topological types
nodes.origin_citation: Perelman, Ricci Flow with Surgery on Three-Manifolds

nodes.name: Existence of well-defined surgery (Claim 2)
nodes.statement: There is a well-defined way to perform surgery on $M$ which yields a smooth post-surgery manifold $M'$ with Riemannian metric $g'$.
assumptions: Ricci flow on $M$ blowing up at finite time $T$
Geometric structure of $U$ near singularity from Claim 1
conclusions: A canonical surgery procedure produces $(M', g')$
nodes.origin_citation: Perelman, Ricci Flow with Surgery on Three-Manifolds

nodes.name: Surgery times do not accumulate (Claim 3)
nodes.statement: One can arrange the surgery procedure so that the surgery times do not accumulate.
assumptions: Ricci flow with surgery defined as in Claim 2
conclusions: Surgery times have no accumulation point
Ricci flow with surgery is defined for all time
nodes.origin_citation: Perelman, Ricci Flow with Surgery on Three-Manifolds

nodes.name: Finite extinction in simply-connected case (Claim 4)
nodes.statement: If the original manifold $M$ is simply-connected, then any Ricci flow with surgery on $M$ becomes extinct in finite time.
conclusions: Manifold becomes empty after some finite time

nodes.name: Hyperbolic limit of $w$-thick part (Claim 5)
nodes.statement: There is a finite collection $\{(H_i, x_i)\}_{i=1}^k$ of complete pointed finite-volume hyperbolic $3$-manifolds with constant sectional curvature $-\frac14$ and, for large $t$, maps $f_t : \bigsqcup_i B(x_i, 1/\alpha(t)) \to M_t$ that are $\alpha(t)$-close to isometries, whose image contains $M^+(\alpha(t),t)$, and that send cuspidal tori incompressibly into $M_t$.
assumptions: Ricci flow with surgery on closed orientable $3$-manifold $M$, all components having a point of strictly negative scalar curvature
conclusions: The $w$-thick part approaches a finite-volume hyperbolic $3$-manifold of constant curvature $-1/4$ (with rescaled metric $\widehat{g}(t) = g(t)/t$) with incompressible cuspidal tori
nodes.origin_citation: Perelman, Ricci Flow with Surgery on Three-Manifolds

nodes.name: Thin part is a graph manifold (Claim 6)
nodes.statement: Let $Y_t$ be the truncation of $\bigcup_i H_i$ obtained by removing horoballs at distance approximately $\frac{1}{2\alpha(t)}$ from the basepoints. Then for large $t$, $M_t - f_t(Y_t)$ is a graph manifold.
conclusions: Complement of the hyperbolic image is a graph manifold for large $t$
nodes.origin_citation: Perelman, Ricci Flow with Surgery; Shioya-Yamaguchi

nodes.name: $\kappa$-solution model at high curvature (Claim 7)
nodes.statement: If $R(x,t)$ is large in a Ricci flow on a finite time interval, then in the time-$t$ slice there is a ball centered at $x$ of radius comparable to $R(x,t)^{-1/2}$ in which the geometry is close to that of a ball in a $\kappa$-solution.
assumptions: Ricci flow solution on finite time interval
conclusions: Local geometry near $(x,t)$ is close to that of a $\kappa$-solution at curvature scale $R(x,t)^{-1/2}$

nodes.name: Classification of $3$-dimensional $\kappa$-solutions (Claim 8)
nodes.statement: Any three-dimensional oriented $\kappa$-solution is one of: (a) a finite isometric quotient of the round shrinking $S^3$; (b) a Ricci flow on $S^3$ or $\R P^3$; (c) a standard shrinking round neck on $\R \times S^2$; (d) a Ricci flow on a manifold diffeomorphic to $\R^3$, asymptotically necklike at infinity; (e) the $\Z_2$-quotient $\R \times_{\Z_2} S^2$ of a shrinking round neck.
conclusions: $(M_\infty, g_\infty)$ falls into one of five explicit classes (a)-(e)
nodes.origin_citation: Perelman, Ricci Flow with Surgery on Three-Manifolds

nodes.name: $\mathcal{F}$-functional
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{F}(g, f) = \int_M \left( R + |\nabla f|^2 \right) e^{-f} \, dV$ on $\mathcal{M} \times C^\infty(M)$.

nodes.name: First variation of $\mathcal{F}$
nodes.statement:

conclusions: The displayed first-variation formula

nodes.name: Proof of first variation of $\mathcal{F}$
nodes.statement:
Direct computation using $\delta R = -	riangle v + 
abla_i 
abla_j v_{ij} - R_{ij} v_{ij}$, $\delta(dV) = (v/2) dV$, and integration-by-parts identities involving $	riangle e^{-f} = (|

nodes.name: $\lambda$-invariant
nodes.statement: $\lambda(g) = \mathcal{F}(g, \overline{f})$ where $\overline{f}$ is the unique minimizer of $\mathcal{F}(g, \cdot)$ subject to $\int_M e^{-f} dV = 1$. Equivalently $\lambda(g)$ is the smallest eigenvalue of $-4\triangle + R$.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of $\mathcal{F}$-minimizer
nodes.statement: Given a metric $g$, there is a unique minimizer $\overline{f}$ of $\mathcal{F}(g, f)$ under $\int_M e^{-f} dV = 1$.
conclusions: Unique minimizer $\overline{f}$ exists; $e^{-\overline{f}/2}$ is the positive ground-state eigenvector of $-4\triangle + R$

nodes.name: Monotonicity of $\lambda$ under Ricci flow
nodes.statement: If $g(\cdot)$ is a Ricci flow solution, then $\lambda(g(t))$ is nondecreasing in $t$.
assumptions: $g(\cdot)$ a Ricci flow solution on $[t_1, t_2]$ on closed $M$
conclusions: $\lambda(g(t_1)) \le \lambda(g(t_2))$

nodes.name: Proof of monotonicity of $\lambda$
nodes.statement: Solve backward heat equation $u_t = -\triangle u + Ru$ from $u(t_2) = e^{-\overline{f}(t_2)}$ to obtain $f(t)$ with $\int e^{-f(t)} dV = 1$; apply $\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal{F}(g(t), f(t)) \ge 0$ from variational identity.

nodes.name: Steady breather
nodes.statement: A Ricci flow solution on $[t_1, t_2]$ satisfying $g(t_2) = \phi^* g(t_1)$ for some $\phi \in \Diff(M)$.

nodes.name: Steady breather is a gradient steady soliton
nodes.statement: On compact $M$, a steady breather is a gradient steady soliton.
conclusions: $R_{ij} + \nabla_i \nabla_j f = 0$ for some $f$

nodes.name: $\mathcal{W}$-functional
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{W}(g, f, \tau) = \int_M \left[ \tau (|\nabla f|^2 + R) + f - n \right] (4\pi\tau)^{-n/2} e^{-f} dV$ on $\mathcal{M} \times C^\infty(M) \times \R^+$.

nodes.name: $\mu$ and $\nu$ invariants
nodes.statement: $\mu(g, \tau) = \inf_f \{ \mathcal{W}(g, f, \tau) : \int_M (4\pi\tau)^{-n/2} e^{-f} dV = 1 \}$.

nodes.name: Locally collapsing Ricci flow
nodes.statement: A Ricci flow $g(\cdot)$ on $[0,T)$ is locally collapsing at $T$ if there exist $t_k \to T$ and balls $B_k = B(p_k, r_k)$ at times $t_k$ with $r_k^2/t_k$ bounded, $|\Rm|(g(t_k)) \le r_k^{-2}$ in $B_k$, and $\lim_{k\to\infty} r_k^{-n} \vol(B_k) = 0$.

nodes.name: $\kappa$-noncollapsed metric on scale $\rho$ (Definition I.4.2)
nodes.statement: A metric $g$ is $\kappa$-noncollapsed on the scale $\rho$ if every metric ball $B$ of radius $r < \rho$ with $|\Rm(x)| \le r^{-2}$ for every $x \in B$ satisfies $\vol(B) \ge \kappa r^n$.

nodes.name: $\kappa$-noncollapsed Ricci flow on scale $\rho$ (parabolic version)
nodes.statement: A Ricci flow $g(\cdot)$ on $[0,T)$ is $\kappa$-noncollapsed on scale $\rho$ if for each $r<\rho$ and $(x_0, t_0)$ with $t_0 \ge r^2$, whenever $|\Rm(x,t)| \le r^{-2}$ on the parabolic region $B_{t_0}(x_0,r) \times [t_0-r^2, t_0]$, then $\vol(B_{t_0}(x_0,r)) \ge \kappa r^n$.

nodes.name: No local collapsing theorem I (Theorem I.4.1)
nodes.statement: If $M$ is closed and $T < \infty$, then a Ricci flow solution $g(\cdot)$ on $[0,T)$ is not locally collapsing at $T$.
conclusions: $g(\cdot)$ is not locally collapsing at $T$; equivalently, $g(\cdot)$ is $\kappa$-noncollapsed on some scale $\rho$ for $\kappa = \kappa(g(0), T, \rho)$

nodes.name: Proof of no local collapsing I
nodes.statement: By contradiction using monotonicity of $\mu(g(\cdot), \tau)$ and a test function $\Phi_k(x) = e^{-c_k/2} \phi(\dist_{t_k}(x,p_k)/r_k)$ that drives $\mathcal{W}(g(t_k), f_k, r_k^2) \to -\infty$ in the collapsing case, contradicting continuity of $\mu(g(0), \tau)$.

nodes.name: Set up test function $\Phi_k$
nodes.statement: Define $\Phi_k(x) = e^{-c_k/2} \phi(\dist_{t_k}(x,p_k)/r_k)$ with bump $\phi$ supported in $[0,1]$, normalized by $e^{c_k} = \int_M (4\pi r_k^2)^{-n/2} \phi^2(\dist_{t_k}(x,p_k)/r_k) dV$, so $c_k \to -\infty$ in the collapsing case.

nodes.name: Bound $\mathcal{W}(g(t_k), f_k, r_k^2) \to -\infty$
nodes.statement: Use Bishop-Gromov (Ricci lower bound) plus scalar-curvature upper bound to show $\mathcal{W}(g(t_k), f_k, r_k^2) \le \const + c_k \to -\infty$.

nodes.name: Apply monotonicity of $\mu$
nodes.statement: By Proposition I.3.1 (monotonicity of $\mu$), $\mu(g(0), t_k + r_k^2) \le \mu(g(t_k), r_k^2) \to -\infty$, contradicting continuity of $\tau \mapsto \mu(g(0), \tau)$.

nodes.name: Conclude contradiction
nodes.statement: Combine to derive contradiction with continuity of $\mu(g(0), \cdot)$, proving the theorem.

nodes.name: No local collapsing theorem II
nodes.statement: Given $n, T < \infty$ and $\rho, K, c > 0$, there exists $\kappa = \kappa(n,K,c,\rho,T) > 0$ such that every Ricci flow on $[0,T)$ with bounded curvature on compact subintervals and initial data $(M, g(0))$ complete with $|\Rm| \le K$ and $\inj(M, g(0)) \ge c$ is $\kappa$-noncollapsed on scale $\rho$.
assumptions: $(M^n, g(\cdot))$ Ricci flow on $[0,T)$, $|\Rm|$ bounded on compact subintervals
$(M,g(0))$ complete with $|\Rm| \le K$ and $\inj(M, g(0)) \ge c$
conclusions: Solution is $\kappa$-noncollapsed on scale $\rho$ in the parabolic sense (Definition I.4.2 parabolic)
$\kappa$ may be chosen nonincreasing in $T$

nodes.name: Reduced length and reduced volume ($\mathcal{L}$-geometry)
nodes.statement: For a backward parameter $\tau = t_0 - t$ and basepoint $(x_0, t_0)$, the $\mathcal{L}$-length of a curve $\gamma$ is $\mathcal{L}(\gamma) = \int_0^{\bar\tau} \sqrt{\tau} (R + |\dot\gamma|^2) d\tau$. The reduced length is $\ell(q, \tau) = L(q, \tau)/(2\sqrt{\tau})$ where $L(q,\tau)$ is the $\mathcal{L}$-distance, and the reduced volume is $\widetilde{V}(\tau) = \int_M (4\pi\tau)^{-n/2} e^{-\ell(q,\tau)} dV(q)$.

nodes.name: Pseudolocality theorem (Theorem I.10.1)
nodes.statement: For every $\alpha > 0$ there exist $\delta, \epsilon > 0$ such that for any pointed Ricci flow solution $(M, (x_0, 0), g(\cdot))$ on $[0, (\epsilon r_0)^2]$ with complete time slices, if $R(x,0) \ge -r_0^{-2}$ and $\vol(\partial \Omega)^n \ge (1-\delta) c_n \vol(\Omega)^{n-1}$ on $B_0(x_0, r_0)$, then $|\Rm|(x,t) < \alpha t^{-1} + (\epsilon r_0)^{-2}$ whenever $0 < t \le (\epsilon r_0)^2$ and $\dist_t(x, x_0) \le \epsilon r_0$.
assumptions: Ricci flow $(M,g(\cdot))$ on $[0,(\epsilon r_0)^2]$ with complete time slices
Almost-Euclidean isoperimetric inequality $\vol(\partial \Omega)^n \ge (1-\delta) c_n \vol(\Omega)^{n-1}$ for $\Omega \subset B_0(x_0,r_0)$
conclusions: $|\Rm|(x,t) < \alpha t^{-1} + (\epsilon r_0)^{-2}$ for $\dist_t(x, x_0) \le \epsilon r_0$, $0 < t \le (\epsilon r_0)^2$

nodes.name: Proof of pseudolocality
nodes.statement: Argument by contradiction: pick a first bad point $(\overline x, \overline t)$, use the conjugate heat kernel $u$ and auxiliary $v$, derive a negative upper bound for $\int_B v\,dV$ (Claims 1-3), then combine with the logarithmic Sobolev inequality (which follows from the almost-Euclidean isoperimetric inequality) to get a contradiction.

nodes.name: Point-selection (Claim 1)
nodes.statement: Find $(\overline x, \overline t) \in M_\alpha = \{|\Rm| \ge \alpha t^{-1}\}$ such that all nearby points $(x', t')$ with $t' \le \overline t$ satisfy $|\Rm(x', t')| \le 4 |\Rm(\overline x, \overline t)|$.

nodes.name: Establish parabolic regions (Claim 2)
nodes.statement: Use Claim 1 to get controlled curvature in a forward parabolic neighborhood of $(\overline x, \overline t)$.

nodes.name: Negative upper bound on $\int_B v\,dV$ (Claim 3)
nodes.statement: By contradiction with rescaled limits, obtain a strictly negative upper bound on $\int_B v\,dV$ at a time near $\overline t$.

nodes.name: Conclude via log Sobolev / isoperimetric inequality
nodes.statement: Apply the localized differential Harnack inequality to push the negative bound back to $t=0$; contradict with the log Sobolev inequality implied by the almost-Euclidean isoperimetric assumption.

nodes.name: Localized differential Harnack inequality (Proposition I.9.1)
nodes.statement:
If $u = (4\pi(T-t))^{-n/2} e^{-f}$ satisfies $\square^* u = 0$ and $v = [(T-t)(2	riangle f - |
abla f|^2 + R) + f - n] u$, then $\square^* v = -2(T-t) |R_{ij} + 
abla_i 
abla_j f - g_{ij}/(2(T-t))|^2 u$ where $\square^* = -\partial_t - 	riangle + R$.
conclusions: The displayed pointwise identity for $\square^* v$

nodes.name: $\kappa$-solution
nodes.statement: A $\kappa$-solution is a Ricci flow $(M, g(\cdot))$ defined on $(-\infty, C)$ (or $(-\infty, C]$) such that: (i) $|\Rm|$ is bounded on each compact time interval and each time slice is complete; (ii) the curvature operator is nonnegative and scalar curvature is everywhere positive; (iii) the flow is $\kappa$-noncollapsed at all scales.

nodes.name: Existence of asymptotic soliton (Proposition I.11.2)
nodes.statement: For any $\kappa$-solution $(M, g(\cdot))$ and basepoint $(p, t_0)$, there is a sequence $\overline{\tau}_i \to \infty$ such that the parabolic rescaling of $g(\cdot)$ at $(q(\overline{\tau}_i), t_0 - \overline{\tau}_i)$ by factor $\overline{\tau}_i^{-1}$ converges (on $[-1, -1/2]$) to a nonflat gradient shrinking soliton.
conclusions: Limit is a nonflat gradient shrinking soliton (the asymptotic soliton)

nodes.name: Compactness of three-dimensional $\kappa$-solutions (Theorem I.11.7)
nodes.statement: For any $\kappa > 0$, the space of pointed three-dimensional oriented $\kappa$-solutions, normalized so that scalar curvature equals $1$ at the basepoint, is compact in the smooth pointed topology.
assumptions: Sequence of pointed $3$D oriented $\kappa$-solutions normalized to have $R = 1$ at basepoint
conclusions: A subsequence converges smoothly to another pointed $\kappa$-solution

nodes.name: Universal $\kappa_0$ (Proposition I.11.9)
nodes.statement: There is a universal $\kappa_0 > 0$ such that any three-dimensional $\kappa$-solution which is not a finite isometric quotient of the round shrinking $S^3$ is in fact a $\kappa_0$-solution.
assumptions: $(M, g(\cdot))$ a $3$D $\kappa$-solution not isometric to a finite quotient of the round shrinking $S^3$
conclusions: $(M, g(\cdot))$ is $\kappa_0$-noncollapsed for a universal $\kappa_0$

nodes.name: $\Phi$-almost nonnegative curvature
nodes.statement: Let $\Phi \in C^\infty(\R)$ be positive nondecreasing with $\Phi(s)/s$ decreasing to $0$ as $s \to \infty$. A Ricci flow has $\Phi$-almost nonnegative curvature if $\Rm(x,t) \ge -\Phi(R(x,t))$ for all $(x,t)$.

nodes.name: Canonical neighborhood theorem (Theorem I.12.1)
nodes.statement: Given $\epsilon, \kappa, \sigma > 0$ and a function $\Phi$ as above, there exists $r_0 > 0$ with the following property: if $g(\cdot)$ is a Ricci flow on a $3$-manifold $M$ defined for $0 \le t \le T$ with $T \ge 1$, complete time slices, $\Phi$-almost nonnegative curvature, and $\kappa$-noncollapsed on scales $< \sigma$, then for any $(x_0, t_0)$ with $t_0 \ge 1$ and $Q = R(x_0, t_0) \ge r_0^{-2}$, the parabolic neighborhood $\{(x,t) : \dist_{t_0}^2(x,x_0) < (\epsilon Q)^{-1}, t_0 - (\epsilon Q)^{-1} \le t \le t_0\}$ is, after scaling by $Q$, $\epsilon$-close to the corresponding subset of a $\kappa$-solution.
assumptions: $3$D Ricci flow $g(\cdot)$ on $[0,T]$, $T \ge 1$, complete time slices
conclusions: For any high-curvature spacetime point $(x_0, t_0)$ with $R(x_0,t_0) \ge r_0^{-2}$, the rescaled local geometry is $\epsilon$-close to that of a $\kappa$-solution

nodes.name: Proof of canonical neighborhood theorem
nodes.statement: By contradiction with a sequence of bad points $(\hat x_k, \hat t_k)$. Four steps: (1) replace by carefully selected sequence $(x_k, t_k)$ where higher-curvature nearby points are 'good'; (2)-(4) build a $\kappa$-solution from rescaled limits, contradicting the badness.

nodes.name: Point selection (Step 1)
nodes.statement: Replace bad sequence $(\hat x_k, \hat t_k)$ by $(x_k, t_k)$ such that points of distinctly higher curvature near $(x_k, t_k)$ are 'good'.

nodes.name: Build limit time slice (Step 2)
nodes.statement: Take pointed limit of $(M_k, x_k, \bar g_k(t_k))$ to construct the final time slice $(M_\infty, x_\infty, \bar g_\infty(t_0))$ of the would-be $\kappa$-solution; cone-blowup contradicts curvature blowup on fixed-radius balls.

nodes.name: Extend backwards in time (Step 3)
nodes.statement: Use $\Phi$-almost nonnegative curvature, $\kappa$-noncollapsing, and Hamilton compactness to extend the limit backwards over a time interval.

nodes.name: Conclude $\kappa$-solution (Step 4)
nodes.statement: Show the limit is an ancient $\kappa$-noncollapsed Ricci flow with nonnegative curvature operator; this is the desired $\kappa$-solution, contradicting the badness of $(x_k, t_k)$.

nodes.name: Later scalar curvature bounds on bigger balls (Theorem I.12.2)
nodes.statement: For any $A < \infty$, there exist $K(A) < \infty$ and $\rho(A) > 0$ such that if a $3$D Ricci flow has $\Phi$-almost nonnegative curvature, $r_0^2 \Phi(r_0^{-2}) < \rho$, $|\Rm|(x,t) \le 1/(3 r_0^2)$ on $\{\dist_0(x, x_0) < r_0\} \times [0, r_0^2]$, and $\vol(B(x_0, r_0)) \ge A^{-1} r_0^3$ at $t=0$, then $R(x, r_0^2) \le K r_0^{-2}$ whenever $\dist_{r_0^2}(x, x_0) < A r_0$.
conclusions: $R(x, r_0^2) \le K(A) r_0^{-2}$ for all $x$ with $\dist_{r_0^2}(x, x_0) < A r_0$

nodes.name: Earlier scalar curvature bounds on smaller balls (Theorem I.12.3)
nodes.statement: Curvature/volume bounds at a later time, together with $\Phi$-almost nonnegativity, propagate backward to give scalar curvature bounds on smaller balls at earlier times in the indicated parabolic neighborhood.
assumptions: Curvature/volume hypotheses analogous to Theorem I.12.2 with roles of past/future swapped
conclusions: Earlier-time scalar curvature bound on smaller ball

nodes.name: Thick-thin decomposition for nonsingular flows (Theorem I.13.1)
nodes.statement: Let $g(\cdot)$ be a Ricci flow on a closed oriented $3$-manifold $M$ existing for $t \in [0, \infty)$ with sectional curvatures $\ge -1$ at $t=0$. There exist $T(w) > 0$, $\overline\rho(w) > 0$, $K(w) < \infty$ such that if $t \ge T$ and $x \in M_{thick}(w, t)$, then $|\Rm| \le K t^{-1}$ on $B_t(x, \overline\rho \sqrt{t})$ and $\vol(B_t(x, \overline\rho \sqrt{t})) \ge \frac{1}{10} w (\overline\rho \sqrt{t})^3$.
conclusions: Curvature and volume bounds on the thick part for large $t$, in scale $\sqrt{t}$

nodes.name: Standard solution
nodes.statement: A standard solution is a Ricci flow on $\R^3$ starting from a fixed rotationally symmetric, asymptotically cylindrical, complete metric of bounded nonnegative curvature, evolving for $t \in [0, 1)$.

nodes.name: Ricci flow with surgery
nodes.section: Section: Ricci flow with surgery, the general setting
nodes.statement: A Ricci flow with surgery is given by: (i) a collection of Ricci flows $\{(M_k \times [t_k^-, t_k^+), g_k(\cdot))\}_{k=1}^N$ with $t_k^+ = t_{k+1}^-$ and $g_k$ going singular at $t_k^+$ for $k<N$; (ii) limits $\{(\Omega_k, \bar g_k)\}$ at the singular times; and (iii) isometric embeddings $\psi_k : X_k^+ \to X_{k+1}^-$ of compact submanifolds-with-boundary identifying the surviving regions across surgery times.

nodes.name: Canonical neighborhood (II.4.1)
nodes.statement: A Ricci flow with surgery $\M$ on $[a,b]$ satisfies the $r$-canonical neighborhood assumption (for nonincreasing $r : [a,b] \to (0,\infty)$) if every $(x,t) \in \M_t^\pm$ with $R(x,t) \ge r(t)^{-2}$ has an open neighborhood $U \subset \M_t^\pm$ that is one of: (a) a strong $\epsilon$-neck; (b) an $\epsilon$-cap; (c) an $\epsilon$-round component; (d) an $\epsilon$-close approximation of a part of a standard solution.

nodes.name: $\Phi$-pinching ($a$ priori assumption I)
nodes.statement: A Ricci flow with surgery satisfies $\Phi$-pinching if at each spacetime point, $\Rm \ge -\Phi(R)$ in the sense of Definition (I.12).

nodes.name: A priori assumptions (II.4.1)
nodes.statement: The a priori assumptions on a Ricci flow with surgery $\M$ on $[a,b]$ consist of: (1) $\Phi$-pinching, and (2) the $r$-canonical neighborhood assumption with respect to a chosen function $r$.

nodes.name: Ricci flow with $(r, \delta)$-cutoff
nodes.statement: A Ricci flow with surgery in which surgeries are performed only at the centers of $\delta$-necks contained in $\epsilon$-horns of $\Omega$, with surgery scale parameter $h$ controlled by $r$ and $\delta$, and capped off by gluing in standard caps; the surgery procedure is determined by the functions $r$ and $\delta$.

nodes.name: Normalized initial condition
nodes.statement: A compact Riemannian $3$-manifold is normalized if $|\Rm| \le 1$ everywhere and the volume of every unit ball is at least half the volume of the Euclidean unit ball.

nodes.name: Existence of Ricci flow with surgery for all time (Proposition II.5.1)
nodes.statement: There exist decreasing sequences $0 < r_j < \epsilon^2$, $\kappa_j > 0$, $0 < \bar\delta_j < \epsilon^2$ for $1 \le j < \infty$ such that for any normalized initial data and any nonincreasing $\delta : [0,\infty) \to (0,\infty)$ with $\delta < \bar\delta_j$ on $[2^{j-1}\epsilon, 2^j \epsilon]$, the Ricci flow with $(r,\delta)$-cutoff is defined for all time and is $\kappa$-noncollapsed at scales $< \epsilon$.
assumptions: Sequence parameters $(r_j, \bar\delta_j, \kappa_j)$ chosen by induction on $j$
conclusions: Ricci flow with $(r,\delta)$-cutoff is defined for all $t \in [0, \infty)$
Resulting flow is $\kappa$-noncollapsed on scales $< \epsilon$

nodes.name: Proof of existence of Ricci flow with surgery (Prop II.5.1)
nodes.statement: Induction on $j$: assuming the conclusion holds on $[0, 2^j \epsilon]$, choose $r_{j+1}, \kappa_{j+1}, \bar\delta_{j+1}$ (and adjust $\bar\delta_j$) so it holds on $[0, 2^{j+1}\epsilon]$. Two main ingredients each step: (a) extend $\kappa$-noncollapsing using a localized $L$-geometry/reduced volume argument that survives surgeries (Lemma II.5.2 = Lemma \ref{II.5.2}); (b) extend the canonical neighborhood assumption via blowup analysis combined with closeness to either a $\kappa$-solution or a standard solution.

nodes.name: Inductive setup
nodes.statement: Suppose $r_i, \bar\delta_i, \kappa_i$ for $i \le j$ chosen so the proposition holds on $[0, 2^j \epsilon]$. Goal: choose $r_{j+1}, \kappa_{j+1}, \bar\delta_{j+1}$ (and possibly adjust $\bar\delta_j$) for $[0, 2^{j+1}\epsilon]$.

nodes.name: Noncollapsing in presence of surgery (Lemma II.5.2)
nodes.statement: Use the $L$-function adapted to surgeries: by making $\delta$ small near surgery times, force $\mathcal{L}$-length of any curve passing close to the surgery locus to be large; then the noncollapsing argument of Theorem I.7.3 goes through, using a base time slice in $[2^{j-1}\epsilon, 2^j \epsilon]$ rather than near $0$.

nodes.name: Canonical neighborhood assumption (Proposition II.6.3 etc.)
nodes.statement: Argue by contradiction (analogous to Theorem I.12.1) that on $[2^j \epsilon, 2^{j+1}\epsilon]$ every $(x,t)$ with $R(x,t) \ge r_{j+1}^{-2}$ has an $\epsilon$-canonical neighborhood; the blowup either gives a $\kappa$-solution (via I.12.1-style argument) or a standard solution (when surgery is nearby in past).

nodes.name: Surgeries do not accumulate
nodes.statement: Each surgery at time $t$ removes a definite volume $v(t) > 0$ proportional to a power of the surgery scale $h(t)$; combined with controlled volume growth this rules out accumulation of surgery times in any bounded interval.

nodes.name: Conclude induction step
nodes.statement: Combine noncollapsing, canonical neighborhood assumption, and finiteness of surgery times in $[2^j\epsilon, 2^{j+1}\epsilon]$ to conclude the proposition on $[0, 2^{j+1}\epsilon]$.

nodes.name: Forcing $\mathcal{L}_+$ to be large (Lemma II.5.3)
nodes.section: Establishing noncollapsing in presence of surgery
nodes.statement: By choosing the surgery parameter $\delta$ small enough at time $t'$, the $\mathcal{L}$-length of any admissible curve passing close to the time-$t'$ surgery locus is forced to be large, provided the endtime $t_0$ of the curve is not too large compared to $t'$.
conclusions: For $\delta(t')$ sufficiently small, any admissible curve from $(x_0, t_0)$ passing near the surgery locus has $\mathcal{L}$-length $\ge L_0$, where $L_0$ depends on $t_0 - t'$

nodes.name: Noncollapsing estimate with surgery (Lemma II.5.2)
nodes.section: Establishing noncollapsing in presence of surgery
nodes.statement: Under the inductive a priori assumptions, the Ricci flow with $(r,\delta)$-cutoff is $\kappa$-noncollapsed on scales $< \epsilon$ in time slab $[2^j \epsilon, 2^{j+1}\epsilon]$, provided $\delta$ is small enough.
assumptions: Inductive a priori assumptions valid through time $2^j \epsilon$
conclusions: $\kappa$-noncollapsing on $[2^j\epsilon, 2^{j+1}\epsilon]$ on scales $< \epsilon$

nodes.name: Thin part is a graph manifold I (Theorem II.7.4 first version)
nodes.statement: Suppose $(M^\alpha, g^\alpha)$ is a sequence of compact oriented Riemannian $3$-manifolds (closed or with convex boundary), $w^\alpha \to 0$, with: (1) for each $x \in M^\alpha$ there is $\rho^\alpha(x) \le \diam(M^\alpha)$ with $\vol(B(x,\rho)) \le w^\alpha \rho^3$ and $\sec \ge -\rho^{-2}$ on $B(x,\rho)$; (2) each boundary component has diameter $\le w^\alpha$ and a topologically trivial collar of length $1$ with sectional curvatures near $-1/4$. Then for large $\alpha$, $M^\alpha$ is diffeomorphic to a graph manifold.
conclusions: For large $\alpha$, $M^\alpha$ is diffeomorphic to a graph manifold

nodes.name: Thin part is a graph manifold II (Theorem II.7.4 second version)
nodes.statement: With hypotheses (1), (2) of Theorem II.7.4 (without the $\rho \le \diam$ restriction) plus (3): bounded covariant derivatives $|\nabla^m \Rm| \le K_m r^{-m-2}$ on balls of low scale and definite volume ratio. Then for large $\alpha$, $M^\alpha$ is diffeomorphic to a graph manifold.
assumptions: Same setup as Theorem II.7.4 first version
Add condition (3): a priori derivative bounds on curvature on balls with definite volume and curvature lower bound
conclusions: For large $\alpha$, $M^\alpha$ is diffeomorphic to a graph manifold

nodes.name: Thin part of long-time Ricci flow with surgery is a graph manifold
nodes.statement: For large $t$, the part $M_{thin}(t) = \M_t^+ - f(t)(\widehat{H}_1(t) \cup \ldots \cup \widehat{H}_k(t))$ of the time-$t$ slice complementary to the truncated hyperbolic image is a graph manifold.
assumptions: Long-time Ricci flow with surgery $\M$ on closed orientable $3$-manifold
conclusions: $M_{thin}(t)$ is diffeomorphic to a graph manifold for large $t$

nodes.name: Incompressibility of cuspidal tori
nodes.statement: Each cuspidal torus of the limiting hyperbolic pieces $H_i$ embeds incompressibly into $M_t$ via the maps $f_t$.
conclusions: Image under $f_t$ of every cuspidal torus is incompressible in $M_t$

nodes.name: Geometrization Conjecture from Ricci flow with surgery
nodes.statement: Combining the existence of Ricci flow with surgery for all time (Proposition II.5.1), the Claim-1 / Claim-2 / Claim-3 surgery package, the long-time hyperbolic-thick limit (Claim 5), incompressibility of cuspidal tori, and the graph-manifold thin-part theorem (Theorem II.7.4), every closed orientable $3$-manifold satisfies Thurston's Geometrization Conjecture.
conclusions: $M$ admits the geometric decomposition asserted by the Geometrization Conjecture

nodes.name: Poincare Conjecture
nodes.statement: Every simply-connected closed $3$-manifold is diffeomorphic to $S^3$.
conclusions: $M$ is diffeomorphic to $S^3$

nodes.name: Proof of Poincare Conjecture from Claims 1-4
nodes.statement: By Claim 4, the Ricci flow with surgery becomes empty in finite time. By Claims 1-3, the original $M$ is a connected sum of factors each diffeomorphic to $S^1 \times S^2$ or a quotient $S^3/\Gamma$. Simple-connectivity and van Kampen's theorem force $M$ to be a connected sum of $S^3$'s, hence $\cong S^3$.

nodes.name: Self-containedness and exposition role
nodes.statement: These notes are intended for readers with a solid background in geometric analysis and follow the section numbering of Perelman's papers I and II to facilitate use as a companion. Cited references for background on Ricci flow include Chow-Knopf, Chow-Lu-Ni, Hamilton, and Topping.

nodes.name: Convention on small/large parameters
nodes.statement: Throughout, conditions like $a > 0$ are read as 'a is a small parameter' and $A < \infty$ as 'A is a large parameter'. The convention is pedagogical and may be ignored.

nodes.name: Definitions of $\kappa$-noncollapsing differ slightly
nodes.statement: The parabolic version of $\kappa$-noncollapsing (Definition I.4.2 parabolic) requires the curvature bound $|\Rm| \le r^{-2}$ on the entire parabolic region $B_{t_0}(x_0,r) \times [t_0-r^2, t_0]$, while the original (Definition I.4.2) only requires it on the final ball. The parabolic notion is stronger as a hypothesis, weaker as a conclusion; for ancient solutions (where $R_t \ge 0$) the two are essentially equivalent.
